summary: Declare metric thresholds in KDL; the daemon evaluates conditions in the background and notifies owners once on breach and recovery.

replay.detail: No graph replay required. Local condition heads seed from indexed latest per-instance state, not historical replay. Replication re-admits old unknown-subject-family invalid records once per schema digest; genuinely invalid records remain invalid and do not retry on every pass.

schema.detail: Adds condition declarations and condition-instance subjects with system-only durable condition.state transitions; routine values stay local. Registry digest expands. Storage version stays 18; five local condition tables and a desired-condition partial index are created on store open, without a global claims-index build.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule changes. Only entry/recovery transitions append durable condition.state; routine samples and intermediate phases stay in a bounded local overlay. Minimum holds and recovery cooldown bound flapping.

compatibility.detail: Additive /v1/conditions and st conditions ls/show. Client-v0 attention_kind adds condition; generated clients and CONTRACT_SHA256 change. Deploy daemons before CLI, every member before publishing new facts, and clients before person-owned conditions. Older schemas reject the new subject families; upgrade retries those rejections once per new digest.

downtime.detail: Ordinary daemon restart; breaches resume silently and pending holds restart. Background evaluation every 30 seconds; hourly physical database sampling; one isolated disk worker with stale-cache diagnostics.

manual.detail: Operations must deploy all fleet daemons before publishing the first conditions. Keep existing watches until real-host breach/recovery verification and operations approval.

recovery.detail: Roll forward after declarations exist. An older daemon cannot evaluate them. Unknown-family records rejected by old registries heal on an upgraded schema; other invalid records require normal replication repair. Durable notification retries are idempotent, limited to three failures per row, and visible in doctor.
